title: The Metal That Melts in Your Hand
hook: Imagine holding a metal that melts in your hand.
script: Imagine holding a metal that melts in your hand. Could a piece of metal really melt just from being held? Gallium, with a melting point of 29.76 degrees Celsius, is unique among metals. This fascinating metal destabilizes at higher temperatures, absorbing heat from your skin. You can even stir gallium into hot tea and watch it vanish completely into the drink. To put this in perspective, gallium melts at a temperature only 7.5 degrees above a warm cup of coffee. Discovered in 1875 by Paul-Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran, gallium challenges our assumptions about metals. So, would you want to hold something that melts in your hand?
